prompt:
Protect the API with keys and roles.
- Requests carry `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Keys live in the data as `apiKeys: [{ "key", "name", "role" }]`; add one key per role to data/seed.json.
- Roles: `viewer` may only read (GET). `cook` may also cook recipes, record waste, log temperatures and enter stock-take counts. `manager` may do everything.
- A request without a key or with an unknown key is 401; a known key without permission is 403. Both answer in the usual error shape with their own error codes.
- Every request that changes data writes an audit entry (time, key name, method, path, status). `GET /audit` lists them newest first and is for managers only.
Update the existing tests so they send a key.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer:
API keys and roles are in. `npm test` passes (29 tests) and `npm run lint` is ok. I left `data/db.json` unchanged, so the real server answers 401 to every request until you add an `apiKeys` list to that file. The seed has one key per role: `larder-viewer-key`, `larder-cook-key` and `larder-manager-key`.

- **Schema:** this is a schema change, so I bumped `CURRENT_VERSION` to 3. The v2→v3 migration adds empty `apiKeys` and `audit` lists and `seq.audit`.
- **Tests:** `tests/helpers.js` now sends the manager key by default, rather than every test setting a header itself. I added `tests/auth.test.js` covering 401, 403 and the audit trail. `tests/cli.test.js` also changed: its two schema-version expectations went from 2 to 3 because of the bump.
- **Cook role:** it can post to `/recipes/:id/cook`, `/batches/:id/waste`, `/temperatures` and `/stocktakes/:id/counts`. Starting and finishing a stock-take stay manager-only.
- **Audit trail:** every non-GET request from a known key is recorded, whatever its status (including 403 and 4xx errors). Requests that fail authentication (401) aren't recorded, since there is no key name to log. `GET /audit` is manager-only and returns newest first.
- **Docs:** I updated `README.md`, `docs/API.md`, `docs/DATA.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`.

check.why: keys, roles, audit and docs all right
